original_question: If a in R^n has Euclidean norm ||a||_2 = 1, must the probability over a uniform random x in {-1,1}^n satisfy Pr[|<a,x>| <= 1] >= 1/2?
target_in_paper: Tomaszewski’s Conjecture (unnumbered open-problem entry): “Let a ∈ R^n have ||a||_2 = 1. Then Pr_{x∼{-1,1}^n}[|⟨a,x⟩| ≤ 1] ≥ 1/2.” ([cs.cmu.edu](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/papers/aobf-open-problems.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s target almost verbatim: the ambient space is R^n, the hypothesis is ||a||_2 = 1, x is uniformly random in {-1,1}^n, the quantity of interest is |⟨a,x⟩|, the threshold is 1, and the conjectured lower bound is 1/2. It also correctly uses the paper’s non-strict inequality “≤ 1”, rather than the distinct strict-inequality variant mentioned only in the remarks. ([cs.cmu.edu](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/papers/aobf-open-problems.pdf))
missing_details: Make the universal quantifiers explicit: the question is for every positive integer n and every vector a ∈ R^n with ||a||_2 = 1.
Define the operator explicitly so the question is stand-alone: ⟨a,x⟩ = Σ_{i=1}^n a_i x_i.
State explicitly that x is chosen uniformly from {-1,1}^n, equivalently that x_1,...,x_n are independent uniform signs.
Identify it by the paper’s name for the problem: Tomaszewski’s Conjecture. ([cs.cmu.edu](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/papers/aobf-open-problems.pdf))
refined_question: Tomaszewski’s Conjecture: For every positive integer n and every vector a = (a_1,…,a_n) ∈ R^n with Σ_{i=1}^n a_i^2 = 1, if x = (x_1,…,x_n) is chosen uniformly from {-1,1}^n (equivalently, x_1,…,x_n are independent uniform signs), must one have Pr[|⟨a,x⟩| ≤ 1] = Pr[|Σ_{i=1}^n a_i x_i| ≤ 1] ≥ 1/2? ([cs.cmu.edu](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/papers/aobf-open-problems.pdf))
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper’s unnumbered entry “Tomaszewski’s Conjecture” on page 2, and it already reproduces the core mathematics of the official formulation. The paper’s statement is exactly the unit-vector random-sign question with threshold 1 and lower bound 1/2. The only sharpening needed to make it fully stand-alone is to spell out the universal quantifiers and the inner-product notation. The nearby remarks confirm two scope-critical points: the conjecture is specifically about the non-strict event |⟨a,x⟩| ≤ 1, and the constant 1/2 is intended to be sharp; those same remarks distinguish the conjecture from the weaker known strict-inequality bound Pr[|⟨a,x⟩| < 1] ≥ 3/8 under an additional exclusion on the coordinates of a. Because arXiv:1204.6447 is an open-problems list rather than a technical paper with numbered results such as Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3, the page-2 problem statement is the nearest official formulation to preserve. ([cs.cmu.edu](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/papers/aobf-open-problems.pdf))
